payload.claim: `snapshot` connects sqlite3 directly at `dest` and calls `self._db.backup(copy)` in one pass with no atomic write. If the backup raises partway (disk full, process killed, source lock error), `finally` only closes `copy`; it never removes the destination file, so `dest` is left holding a partially-copied or stale-mixed ledger (worse if `dest` already existed from a prior run, since backup overwrites page-by-page rather than replacing the file). The codebase's own pattern for exactly this hazard is write-to-temp-then-`os.replace` (`saffron/projection.py:510-518`, `saffron/report/index.py:413-423`), which this function does not use. A later `SA-0272` history-command read of that partial file would silently see an incomplete ledger, the same silent-data-loss failure mode (`SA-0107`'s 75-of-76 miss) this backlog item cites as the motivation.
